**Sundhedsklynge Nord** is a local healthcare cluster (sundhedsklynge) operating within [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] in Denmark [^src5]. It serves as one of the primary organizational units monitored by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) to evaluate, benchmark, and improve the quality of care for patients diagnosed with [[atrieflimren|atrial fibrillation]] [^src1]. 

The cluster's clinical performance is tracked across a wide array of national quality indicators. Notably, Sundhedsklynge Nord successfully met the national standard for Indikator 1, achieving a 92.7% result for the timely initiation of anticoagulation therapy in newly diagnosed patients [^src1]. However, the cluster fell short of the ≥ 90% standard for longer-term treatment coverage metrics, recording 88.2% for both 1-year (Indikator 4a1) and 2-year (Indikator 4a2) coverage [^src2], and 85.3% for 5-year coverage (Indikator 4a3) [^src3]. In the subsequent 2025 reporting period, the cluster's implementation of structured patient education (Indikator 8) was measured at 17.3%, indicating a significant area for quality improvement [^src9].

Beyond treatment adherence, Sundhedsklynge Nord is closely monitored for adverse clinical outcomes and epidemiological trends. The geographic incidence of ischemic stroke (apopleksi) among the cluster's atrial fibrillation patients is mapped as part of [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]], contributing to national variance analyses [^src4]. The cluster also routinely reports data on mortality, severe bleeding incidents, and heart failure outcomes, providing critical insights that help health authorities identify case-mix effects and regional disparities in cardiovascular care [^src5], [^src6], [^src7].
